10.0.s.en: (1) The Father's pleasure in the sacrifice of the Son

10.0.0.en: The Law and all the worship of the Old Testament signify the grace of God in the Church of the New Testament, which we receive in the Holy Sacraments and the means of grace. Consequently, the Law cannot, by animal sacrifices, cleanse and justify those who offer them.

10.1.0.en: "Should have had no more conscience of sins": they would no longer fear the punishment of sin.

10.1.1.en: The blood sacrifices offered by the priests and the Levites were for cleansing their hearts from every sin, and they had to be repeated; once was not enough, because they are a type of the complete cleansing by the blood of Christ.

10.2.0.en: He draws them on by saying that the sacrifices are repeated every year, which is proof of their inability to cleanse hearts from sin. The blood of animals is unable to cleanse men from their sins; it is merely a symbol.

10.3.0.en: David the prophet speaks in the spirit of prophecy in (Ps 40:6) about Christ at His incarnation and His coming into the world. The Son says to the Father that You do not desire animal sacrifices, for they are merely a symbol, but You desire the sacrifice of my body, which I offer on the Cross; therefore You have prepared me a body by my birth from the Virgin.

10.4.0.en: "The volume of the book": the ancient books were written on parchments and rolled up, and were called a volume. By "the book" is meant the books of the Old Testament, which prophesied of the coming of Christ.

10.4.1.en: Christ, the incarnate One of whom the prophecies spoke, would become incarnate in the fullness of time to do the will of God, which is redemption on the Cross.

10.5.1.en: As the Psalm (40:6) mentioned previously that God had no pleasure in animal sacrifices, so Paul warns the Hebrews that these sacrifices are merely symbols, so that they would not cling to them.

10.6.0.en: Since God has no pleasure in animal sacrifices but in the sacrifice of Christ, God by this takes away the symbolic animal sacrifices and establishes the sacrifice of Christ, in which the Hebrews must believe, and they must leave behind the old sacrifices.

10.7.0.en: St. Paul the Apostle declares in conclusion that sanctification is accomplished by the will of God, which He fulfilled in the crucifixion of Christ and His redemption of us.

10.7.1.en: We thank God, who has granted us, by partaking of His Body and Blood, forgiveness of our sins and strength to live with Him. May we partake often, as much as we feel our weakness, our need and our love for Him.

10.8.s.en: (2) The salvation of Christ is complete

10.8.0.en: Every Jewish priest stood daily for the priestly service in the Old Testament and offered again the same sacrifices, which were utterly unable to cleanse and to take away sin.

10.9.0.en: "Sat down on the right hand of God": He showed the permanence of His power and His divine glory.

10.9.1.en: The Lord Christ, after He was crucified and offered one sacrifice for the sins of the whole world as an atonement for sins, declared by His ascension His power and glory, by which He saves His children continually.

10.10.0.en: Christ continues to support His children and to rescue them from the wars of the devil, until at the end He brings them into the Kingdom of Heaven and tramples all the power of the devil when He casts him into eternal torment.

10.11.0.en: By the sacrifice of Christ, which is signified by the offerings and sacrifices of the Old Testament, this one sacrifice or offering gives complete salvation to those who believe in Him.

10.12.0.en: The Holy Spirit prophesied beforehand through Jeremiah (Jer 31:32, 33) that after the passing of the Old Testament, and the incarnation of Christ and His redemption, He would establish His word and His commandments in the minds and hearts of those who believe in Him, and this by the work of the Holy Spirit in them and in the Church and through the Holy Sacraments.

10.13.0.en: God forgives the sins of His people through the sacraments of confession and Holy Communion, so that they are completely blotted out from them.

10.14.0.en: After the believers enjoy forgiveness in the Church, they have no need to offer the sacrifices and offerings of the Old Testament.

10.14.1.en: Ask in prayer for the help of the Holy Spirit when you read the words of the Holy Bible, that He may give you understanding of them and make you moved by them, and establish them within you, so that you apply them and live by them, and rejoice in His work in you.

10.15.s.en: (3) Faith and hope in Christ and our love for others

10.15.0.en: In sum, beloved brethren, because we now have boldness to enter into heaven itself by the blood of Christ. He said Jesus alone, without Christ, because He wishes here to stress that He is a representative of men as the Son of Man, to declare the possibility of the redeemed entering heaven by His redemption of us.

10.16.0.en: "The veil": the curtain between the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies, which was a type of Christ. When He was crucified and His body was rent, that is, when He died on the Cross, the veil of the Temple was rent, declaring the completion of salvation and the possibility of man's entering heaven, that is, the highest Holy of Holies, and the possibility of our partaking of His Body and Blood in the Church as a pledge of the Kingdom.

10.16.1.en: By the redemption of Christ, which He recently accomplished on the Cross, He prepared for us the way of the Kingdom, and His body, which He gave on the Cross, He offers to us on the altar every day as a pledge of the Kingdom that He has prepared for us.

10.17.0.en: We also have a greater priest, perfect, holy and without evil, who is Christ, over the house of God, which is the Church and heaven also.

10.18.0.en: He calls us to spiritual growth with pure and sincere hearts, steadfast in faith in Christ the Redeemer, to whom all the sacrifices of the Old Testament point, and that our consciences may be purified by His blood shed for us through the sacrament of repentance and confession, and our bodies washed with the water of Baptism, so that our nature is renewed and we live for Him. This is in place of the sprinkling of the blood of sacrifices to cleanse the defiled and sinners, or their washing with water for cleansing in the Old Testament.

10.19.0.en: "The profession of our hope unwavering": we declare and confess a firm hope.

10.19.1.en: If we have a strong, sincere faith, we can receive a firm hope in Christ, who promises eternal life to everyone who completes his life in faith in Him, steadfast in His holy Church.

10.20.0.en: The Apostle calls us to take care and to encourage one another in our love for others, in serving them and in doing all works of mercy.

10.21.0.en: We must not neglect spiritual gatherings, nor attend them as a mere performance of duty, but use them to teach and exhort one another to grow in the spiritual life in preparation for eternity. Our encouragement of one another increases as much as we sense the approach of the coming of Christ, and that the time of the end of our life in this world is not known.

10.21.1.en: We note here that St. Paul stresses the importance of fellowship and the one body in encouragement and in giving patience in tribulation, since the Christian Hebrews were exposed to persecution from the Jews. So each one's encouraging the other gives steadfastness and patience in faith, for a person feels that there is someone standing beside him in the spiritual striving, and so he is encouraged and made steadfast in his Christ, being persecuted by the Jews.

10.21.2.en: Give me, my God, a spirit of positiveness, that I may stand firm and make those around me firm. Grant that people may see in me a steadfast branch in Your vineyard, so that I draw them by my sweet fruits from the work of Your Holy Spirit. Grant me to remember how much I promised You in the confession of my Baptism, to live with You and to receive You, renouncing all the thoughts of the evil enemy with all steadfastness and without wavering.

10.22.0.en: "If we sin wilfully": this means apostasy from Christianity and returning to Jewish worship because of the persecution by the Jews, and it can also mean persisting in any sin.

10.22.1.en: He warns the believers against apostasy from the Christian faith, because the Jewish animal sacrifices will not profit us, and we will be deprived of the redemption of Christ and His atoning sacrifice.

10.23.0.en: Whoever persists in rejecting Christ has nothing awaiting him but God's judgment of him on the last day, which is a terrible judgment, and He stands against him with great zeal to cast him into the eternal torment prepared for the wicked and those who reject Christ.

10.24.0.en: The Law in which the Jews believe prescribes the putting to death of whoever transgresses it if the sin is proved against him by the testimony of two or three, and no excuse avails or finds pity. This is so that the Law may proclaim the fear of God and respect for the commandment (Mt 18:16).

10.25.0.en: St. Paul shows the hideousness of the sin of him who denies the faith: he treads underfoot Christ and despises His precious redeeming blood by returning to animal sacrifices, and he scorns the grace of the New Testament, which he received in the Holy Sacraments and experienced in his life. If the punishment for transgressing the Law is death, then the rejection of Christ deserves an eternal torment whose hideousness cannot be imagined. And here he declares the divinity of Christ by saying "the Son of God."

10.26.0.en: St. Paul cites the word of God in the Book of Deuteronomy (Deut 32:35, 36), that God judges the wicked and takes vengeance on them. And he uses a human feeling, namely vengeance, to stress the divine punishment of those who reject Him.

10.27.0.en: God is just, living forever and very great; so whoever denies Him and persists in disobeying Him must in the end fall into His hands on the Day of Judgment, and receive a fearful punishment beyond all imagination. After St. Paul persuaded the Jews that all their rites signify Christ, he warns them lest the believer of Jewish origin fall away from Christ and receive an eternal punishment and torment. The Apostle declared all this to rescue those who have fallen away from destruction, that they might return by repentance.

10.27.1.en: Remembering the judgment alerts us to return from our sins and our negligence. God's mercy is for those who fear Him and not for those who despise Him, and our weakness does not hinder His work, but our contempt and persistence in sin is what exposes us to divine punishment.

10.28.0.en: After the severe warning, he softens his words by encouraging them, declaring their virtues, namely their patience in the tribulations they met from non-Christians after their Baptism. Their steadfastness and patience call them to return to Christ and to stand firm in the faith.

10.29.0.en: You were famous for the virtue of endurance of sufferings, and in this you shared with the martyrs and the saints who endured torments, such as Stephen.

10.30.0.en: For I do not forget that you encouraged me during my imprisonment and trial and had compassion on me, and that you even rejoiced when you were subjected to the seizure of your possessions, not caring about what is yours on earth but about the eternal portion you have in heaven, prepared for you, which the moth does not eat and thieves do not steal, as they do the earthly portion.

10.30.1.en: Yes, Lord, teach me not to care about what is mine when it is taken from me for the sake of Your name. Teach me to give up even my lawful right if it hinders me from the glory of Your name, looking to heaven, my original homeland, from which I came, born of You, and to which I shall return to You by Your grace and the work of Your forgiving blood and Your body given for me.

10.31.0.en: Do not neglect your faith in Christ, who grants you blessings on earth and in heaven .. many blessings that cannot be expressed.

10.32.0.en: He calls them to patience in enduring persecutions, encouraging them with the receiving of God's promises of blessing, His support of them during their striving, and their reward in the Kingdom.

10.33.0.en: This is because the Lord will come very soon if we compare our temporary earthly life with the blessed eternity, for the life of men on earth, however long, is nothing before eternity, which has no end. So Christ will come soon and glorify His children with Him in heaven.

10.34.0.en: That you may continue the life of righteousness and holiness, hold fast to your Christian faith. And God declares in (Hab 2:4) that the just shall live by faith. St. Paul the Apostle goes on to make clear God's displeasure with the righteous man if he falls away from his righteousness and his faith, to warn the Christians of Jewish origin lest they fall away from their faith.

10.35.0.en: In conclusion, he encourages them to remain steadfast in the faith by saying that they are not among those who fall away, for whom destruction waits, but that they are steadfast in faith in Christ.

11.0.0.en: St. Paul the Apostle ended the previous chapter with the importance of steadfastness in faith in Christ so that we may endure sufferings and persecutions. And this chapter begins with a definition of faith, saying that it is trust in the power of God, which gives us what we do not see with our eyes now but hope for from His grace, and that this faith is what has distinguished the children of God throughout history since the beginning of creation.

11.1.0.en: We believe first in God, the Creator of all creatures, whether in the world of earth or heaven, and that they came to be out of nothing by the command of God and not out of anything previously existing.

11.1.1.en: If God created everything out of nothing, then He is able to create in me a new heart that loves Him and seeks Him, and to give me an inclination to serve those around me and strength to help them. So I trust in Him and go forward boldly, whatever my weakness.

11.2.s.en: (2) The faith of Abel, Enoch and Noah

11.2.0.en: Abel learned from his father Adam that he would gain God's favor by offering animal sacrifices, just as God slew an animal and clothed his parents with its skin, so that they were covered (Gen 3:21), and taught them that by offering sacrifices they would gain God's favor. Because of Abel's faith and obedience he was justified before God, whereas Cain did not believe God's teaching and offered of the fruits of the ground. Therefore, after Cain killed Abel, his faith continued to bear witness for him (Gen 4:4).

11.3.0.en: Enoch, who was the seventh person from Adam, lived a life pleasing to God, and because of his great godliness God took him up alive to heaven, and he still lives there in a miraculous way, and will come down to earth shortly before the end of days (Gen 5:22, 24). Jesus the son of Sirach testified to his pleasing God (Sir 44:16). (The Book of Jesus the son of Sirach is one of the canonical books which the Protestants removed.)

11.4.0.en: Paul was influenced by the words of Jesus the son of Sirach, and said in this verse that faith is the means to a life pleasing to God, which in the end receives the eternal reward.

11.5.0.en: When God declared to Noah that He would destroy the world by a flood, he believed God's word and made an ark, the building of which took 120 years. It was a means of preaching, that men might repent, but they did not believe, so this ark became a judgment on them, while he was justified by his faith and had a portion in the Kingdom (Gen 6:13, 22).

11.5.1.en: Faith begets obedience to the commandments of God, so receive His commandments however hard they seem, confident of His help, which assists you to carry them out, and your heart will be filled with peace and you will be assured of a blessed eternity.

11.6.0.en: God commanded Abraham to leave his family and his city, Ur of the Chaldeans, which lies between the two rivers in Iraq, and to go out to the wilderness of Canaan, which he did not know, promising him to give it as an inheritance to him and his seed. He believed God's word and obeyed him, and left the populous place where he had lived since his childhood and went out into the unknown, confident that this was the best because it was God's command (Gen 12:1).

11.7.0.en: Despite God's promises to Abraham of the inheritance of the land of Canaan, he did not cling to material goods but lived as a stranger, he and his sons Isaac and Jacob. They dwelt in tents, not built houses, as proof of their being strangers to this world, because they were attached to the abiding city, which is the Kingdom of Heaven, which God founded and which lasts forever.

11.8.0.en: Sarah also believed God's promise to her that she would conceive and bear, although her age had become ninety years and she had lost the human ability to bear children.

11.9.1.en: "As good as dead": Sarah's womb, unable to bear children.

11.9.2.en: God gave Sarah, from her womb, which by reason is considered dead, a son, Isaac, and from him came the people of Israel, great in multitude like the stars of heaven and the sand of the sea.

11.10.0.en: The first fathers believed in the Kingdom of Heaven and that it is the true life with God, so they were strangers to the material things of the world, and took nothing of earthly possessions, and their hearts were attached to eternity, so they passed quickly through this world to reach the Kingdom.

11.11.0.en: The fathers' being strangers to the world declares their faith in another homeland, not earthly, and since they did not cling to the promised land nor to material goods, they declared their attachment to the heavenly homeland. For the sake of this great faith God is not ashamed to be called their God (Ex 3:6), and He prepared for them the heavenly city, that is, the Kingdom of Heaven.

11.12.0.en: God tested Abraham to prove his faith and to show his greatness, and asked him to offer his only son Isaac as a sacrifice. Abraham obeyed, believing that God was able to fulfill His promises of many descendants through Isaac, since God is able to raise from the dead. And just before he slew his son, God stopped him and redeemed him with the ram. Thus the great faith of Abraham appeared, and the sacrifice of Isaac was an example and type of Christ the Redeemer on the Cross: Isaac returned alive because God redeemed him with the ram, but Christ died on the Cross and rose alive on the third day.

11.12.1.en: Your attachment to heaven makes you give up material things easily in order to gain your peace and the peace of those around you, and this increases your spiritual activity, whether in worship or in service.

11.13.s.en: (4) The faith of Isaac, Jacob and Joseph

11.13.0.en: Isaac believed God's promise, at the birth of his children, that the elder would serve the younger (Gen 25:23). So he blessed Jacob his younger son despite his weakness and his lie, and promised him that he would be the father of a great posterity because he would repent and live with God, unlike Esau, who lived far from the worship of God, so Isaac did not give him the blessing he sought.

11.14.0.en: By faith Jacob, the father of the tribes, blessed Manasseh and Ephraim, the sons of Joseph, placing his hands crossed (in the form of a cross) so that his right hand would be on the head of the younger. This was contrary to what was customary, so that Joseph tried to place his father's hands in the usual way, thinking that his father had made a mistake in the placing (Gen 48:18). But Jacob did this by faith, by God's revelation to him that the younger brother would be greater as a people. Therefore he placed his hands in the form of a cross, so that his right hand was on the head of the younger, Ephraim, and his left on the head of the firstborn, Manasseh, worshipping God in his bowing, as if he saw God who made these revelations to him. So he bowed down with the little strength he had, an old man, leaning wholly on the top of his staff.

11.15.0.en: Joseph believed God's promise to Abraham that his seed would be strangers in Egypt and then return to the land of Canaan (Gen 15:14). So despite his great position in Egypt he asked his brothers and their descendants that when they departed from Egypt they take his bones with them, and that was about 400 years after these words.

11.15.1.en: Believe God's promises to you in the Holy Bible, and do not be troubled by the wars of the devil nor occupied with the passing delights of the world, but care for your spiritual life and the salvation of your soul at all times.

11.16.s.en: (5) The faith of Moses and Rahab

11.16.0.en: Despite Pharaoh's command to cast the male children into the river (Ex 1:22), the parents of Moses believed in God's power to preserve them and their son, and hid him three months, against the king's commands.

11.17.0.en: Moses was the son of Pharaoh's daughter, and so was considered the heir to the throne and could become king over Egypt or at least one of the great men of the state. But since he believed in God, he left the palace and went down to share with his people in humiliation and slavery until God would free them, knowing that all earthly lusts and sins pass away, whereas life with God lasts forever.

11.18.0.en: Faith is what lifted Moses above being dazzled by the title of son of Pharaoh's daughter and made him see this humiliation and reproach, which is after the pattern of the Lord Christ's humbling Himself for us from the throne of His glory, as a wealth with which all the treasures of Egypt cannot compare. This is because faith made him not care for temporary wealth but care for the eternal recompense from the hand of God, which is more lasting and better.

11.19.0.en: After God struck the land of Egypt with the ten plagues, Pharaoh yielded to the command of the Lord, and Moses left Egypt with power and did not fear Pharaoh, but on the contrary Pharaoh was afraid of him, because Moses saw God whom Pharaoh did not see. He was able to divide the Red Sea and cross it, while Pharaoh and all his army were drowned (Ex 14).

11.20.0.en: Moses believed God's promise to preserve them from the angel who destroyed the firstborn of Egypt, so he kept the Passover and sprinkled the doorposts with the blood of the Passover lamb as God said, so that the destroying angel would not harm them (Ex 12:21).

11.21.0.en: Moses and the children of Israel believed God's command when he struck the Red Sea, and it divided into two halves and the water became like a wall to the right and to the left. The people crossed in faith on the ground of the sea floor, which had become dry, and reached the other shore. But the hardness of the Egyptians' hearts made them follow them, and when they were all in the sea Moses struck the water and it returned to its place and the whole army of the Egyptians was drowned (Ex 14:22).

11.22.0.en: Jericho, the fortified city that faced the children of Israel under the leadership of Joshua after their crossing of the Jordan River, had its walls fall by the faith of the children of Israel, for all they did was to march around it for seven days as God commanded them (Josh 6:12-20).

11.23.0.en: By faith Rahab, the sinful woman known in the city of Jericho for harlotry, did not perish with those who did not believe. This was because she believed in God and showed her faith by receiving the two spies and not telling the king of Jericho about them, but misleading the king's soldiers who were searching for them (Josh 2:1).

11.23.1.en: Faith makes you not fear the threats of people or the problems that meet you, so trust that your God fights for you and protects you, whatever the power of those who wrong you.

11.24.s.en: (6) The faith of the judges and the prophets

11.24.0.en: St. Paul the Apostle also declares that faith is the foundation of the life of all the saints in the Old Testament and that time is not enough to show their faith. Among their examples are Gideon the judge, who rescued the people of Israel from the Midianites (Judg 6:11); Barak, who delivered the children of Israel from Sisera, the commander of the army of the Canaanites (Judg 4:6); Samson, the vanquisher of the armies of the Philistines (Judg 13:24); Jephthah, who rescued the children of Israel from the children of Ammon (Judg 11:1); David, the righteous king, the psalmist of Israel (1 Sam 16:13); and Samuel, who stood before all the people of Israel when they wished to appoint an earthly king and opposed them by faith, looking to the King of kings and Lord of lords (1 Sam 8:6); and the rest of the prophets, who prophesied by faith about things that had not yet come.

11.25.0.en: St. Paul the Apostle moves from mentioning examples of the heroes of faith to the works of faith, and mentions:

11.25.2.en: 2- "Wrought righteousness": they lived a holy, pure life, such as David.

11.25.3.en: 3- "Obtained promises": by faith they were able to obtain what they were promised, such as Gideon (Judg 8:11).

11.25.4.en: 4- "Stopped the mouths of lions": such as Daniel (Dan 6:22).

11.26.0.en: 5- "Quenched the violence of fire": it could not burn them, such as the Three Youths (Dan 3).

11.26.1.en: 6- "Escaped the edge of the sword": such as Esther and Mordecai (Esth 8).

11.26.2.en: 7- "Out of weakness were made strong": they were strengthened by faith, freed from their human weakness, such as Judith, who triumphed over the armies of the Assyrians (Jdt 14, 15).

11.26.3.en: 8- "Waxed valiant in fight": they became men of might and strength in their wars, such as David and those with him (2 Sam 5:20).

11.26.4.en: 9- "Turned to flight the armies of the aliens": such as Judas Maccabeus and his brothers, who defeated the Greek empire (the First Book of Maccabees).

11.27.0.en: 10- "Women received their dead raised to life again": by faith women were able to enjoy the resurrection of those who had died to them, such as the resurrection of the son of the widow of Zarephath of Sidon, whom Elijah the prophet raised (1 Kgs 17:22).

11.27.1.en: 11- "Others were tortured, not accepting deliverance; that they might obtain a better resurrection": such as the many martyrs in the days of the Maccabees, among them the seven brothers and their mother (2 Macc 7).

11.28.0.en: 12- "Others had trial of cruel mockings": such as the Jews who fought alongside Judas Maccabeus, who after his death were seized and mocked (1 Macc 9:26).

11.28.1.en: 13- "And scourgings": such as the seven brothers in the days of the Maccabees (2 Macc 7:1).

11.28.2.en: 14- "Yea, moreover of bonds and imprisonment": such as Joseph (Gen 39:20) and Jeremiah the prophet (Jer 37:15).

11.29.0.en: "They were stoned": as King Joash commanded the stoning of Zechariah the priest, the son of Jehoiada, because he rebuked the people for their sins that they might return to God (2 Chr 24:21), and Naboth the Jezreelite in the days of Ahab the king (1 Kgs 21:13). "They were sawn asunder": Jewish tradition mentions that Manasseh the king commanded that Isaiah the prophet be sawn asunder.

11.29.1.en: "Were tempted": such as the testing of Abraham by offering Isaac his son as a sacrifice (Gen 22). "Were slain with the sword": such as Ahimelech the priest, whom Saul the king slew because he fed David and gave him the sword and spear of Goliath (1 Sam 22:16). "They wandered about in sheepskins and goatskins; being destitute, afflicted, tormented": such as Elijah the prophet, who lived stripped of possessions (2 Kgs 1:8), and as Micaiah the prophet, whom Ahab the king fed with the bread of affliction in prison, that is, he did not find his necessary food (1 Kgs 22:27).

11.30.0.en: "Of whom the world was not worthy": the heroes of faith mentioned above endured many sufferings for the sake of God and were weak only in appearance, but before God they are saints, higher than the world, and the world does not deserve their presence in it.

11.30.1.en: "They wandered in deserts, and in mountains, and in dens and caves of the earth": some of them lived in the deserts and mountains, keeping away from the evil of the world, which they rebuked, such as Elijah the prophet (1 Kgs 19:9) and John the Baptist (Lk 1:80).

11.31.0.en: All these heroes of faith, to whose faith God bears witness, did not receive the promises on earth, but on the contrary endured many tribulations. But there awaits them, and awaits all of us when we complete our striving, an eternal Kingdom in which we shall enjoy together a happiness that cannot be expressed. They are waiting in the Paradise of Joy, the place of waiting of the righteous, until all the believers enter at one time into the Kingdom of Heaven.

11.31.1.en: The heroes of faith shone because of their striving and their endurance of many labors for God's sake. May we not grow slack in our prayers, our fasts and every good work, but also reject every sin, however pleasant and tempting, confident that our earthly labors are matched by heavenly glories.

11.31.2.en: Striving and serving others to obtain glory
